I built a total beast. Handed an autonomous AI agent the night shift, went to sleep, and it made $832 before I woke up, on a $100 plan.

Every night at 11:40 PM my laptop goes dark and a hummingbird starts working.

That's Hummingbird, my overnight agent. The dashboard is black and white on purpose. A cell only turns colour once the bird has actually touched it. So in the morning I don't read a report. I look at which parts of the screen lit up.

Last night it lit up six jobs:

-> Competitor Watch. 14 platforms, every pricing and release-note change recorded
-> Gig Boards. 86 fresh posts read, anything under budget dropped, the strong ones flagged
-> Agency Reports. Weekly numbers pulled from my tools without sending a single message
-> Mentions Triage. Everything sorted into today, this week or ignore, with replies drafted in my voice
-> Launch Radar. Changelogs scanned so I see new features before my feed does
-> Activity Feed. One clean log of every action and every file it opened

What it's NOT allowed to do matters more than what it does:
- read-only all night
- nothing gets posted or sent without my OK
- 8 safety checks before every step
- if it isn't sure, it holds the job and waits for me

The setup: OpenAI Dots does the reading and clicking, GPT-6 Astra decides what's worth my attention, and a desktop + cloud environment keeps a browser alive while I sleep. It's wired into 4,000+ apps.

I don't write prompts at night. I write one brief before bed and set the rules.

The difference between a chatbot and a night shift is simple: one waits for you, the other is already done when you wake up.

Bookmark this and watch the bird work

What do ChatGPT Dots and Claude Duet actually do all day?

These 6 terms explain how personal agents keep working while you’re offline.

Every big lab has one now: Grok Bot from xAI, Muse from Meta, Dots from OpenAI and, last week, Duet from Anthropic.

Take one example of an agent that reads your inbox overnight and has a brief ready when you open your laptop.

/1 Own computer
The agent gets its own machine in the cloud, with a browser and apps, so it keeps going after you close your laptop. Dots, Grok Bot and Muse each run on one.

/2 Integrations
This is how it reaches your inbox, your calendar and your Slack. Dots connects to 4,000+ apps, and Muse uses integrations to book, shop and pay.

/3 Memory
What it keeps between tasks: who your manager is, which threads you always ignore, what you asked yesterday. Without it, every morning brief starts from zero.

/4 Routines
What starts the work without you asking: a set time, a new email or a Slack mention. Duet's morning brief is a routine.

/5 Approval gates
The moments it has to stop and ask you first. Duet asks before it sends, pays, signs or deletes anything.

/6 Audit log
A record of every action it took, so you can see what happened while you were away. OpenBot, one of the open-source clones, runs every action through a policy check and logs it.

What I haven't seen any launch fully explain yet is:
What happens when a task gets cut off halfway? 
Does it pick up again without sending the same email twice? 
And does your yes on one task carry over to the next? 

Even Anthropic says Duet can still misjudge what's urgent, so I'd test these before connecting an inbox.

Which of these would you want to see before you give an agent your inbox? 👀

I built an absolute monster. My crazy idea to let an autonomous AI agent run wild while I slept made $832 while I was asleep, using just $100.

OpenAI Dots + GPT-6 Astra + 4,000+ apps.

Half a dozen utilities. A single unified ecosystem. Zero human intervention while you're away.

OpenAI Dots -> acts as the core worker, reading everything and touching almost nothing.
GPT-6 Astra -> powers the intellect underneath.
Desktop & Cloud Environment -> keeps a browser and a computer running while your laptop sleeps.
4,000+ Apps -> integrated directly into its workflow.

Before heading to bed, I assigned it a single objective: monitor my competitors, filter incoming leads, triage my inbox, and queue up the morning reports, keeping everything strictly read-only until my approval.

I went to sleep at 11:40 PM, and here is what unfolded over the course of seven hours:

> 12:12 AM: Dots monitors competitor pricing pages and release notes across 14 different platforms, logging every shift in strategy.
> 1:05 AM: It evaluates incoming gig boards, filtering out low budgets and highlighting only the high-value client requests.
> 2:30 AM: It drafts the weekly agency reports, pulling raw numbers directly from connected tools without writing a single unauthorized message.
> 4:10 AM: It runs through my mentions and comments, sorting them into clear action bins (Today, This Week, Drop) and drafting custom replies in my voice.
> 5:45 AM: It compiles a launch radar brief, catching feature updates before they hit the main tech timelines.
> 7:20 AM: It logs every single action, file read, and safety check into a detailed activity feed for my morning review.

Upon waking up, I discovered a fully organized workflow, zero unauthorized changes made to my accounts, and all my morning grunt work completed before my first cup of coffee.

The entire overhead amounted to the flat $100 monthly subscription -- yielding hundreds of hours saved while I slept.

The primary misconception is that individuals turn to AI merely for answers: instead, I provided mine with a clear objective, a strict read-only boundary for the night shift, and a concrete reporting structure.

I did not write a single prompt, nor did I open a single browser tab: I simply went to sleep.

While everyone else is treating AI like a standard chat window, I already have an autonomous worker pulling the night shift.
